plan.title: Capstone lab Task 1 runs activate immediately, skipping the required CAP-DC-01 checkpoint

narratives.Description: Capstone lab Task 1 runs activate immediately, skipping the required CAP-DC-01 checkpoint
narratives.Overview:
## Situation

The capstone curriculum and assessment require a command-free `CAP-DC-01` routing row **before** `activate`:

- `curriculum/capstone-end-to-end.md` CAP.1: “Before `activate`, complete this command-free recognition checkpoint in your private `capstone-assessment-note.md`.”
- `assessments/capstone-end-to-end.md` Task 1: “Run `install` and `orient`. Before `activate`, copy this exact table…”

The lab’s Task 1 command block (`labs/capstone-end-to-end.md`) is:

```sh
node …/capstone-lab.mjs orient "$CAPSTONE_ROOT"
node …/capstone-lab.mjs activate "$CAPSTONE_ROOT"
node …/capstone-lab.mjs ready "$CAPSTONE_ROOT"
```

There is no pause, no note path, and no mention of `CAP-DC-01` between `orient` and `activate`. Expected results are `PASS`, `PASS`, then `READY`.

I completed the capstone on macOS/zsh against 0.119.5. I only inserted the routing row because I had just read the curriculum page. A learner who treats the lab Tasks section as the executable source of truth will activate immediately.

The helper cannot check the private note, so `activate` still prints `PASS` without that checkpoint.

## Pain

CAP.1 is scored on the routing row being captured before activation. Following the lab’s own Task 1 block produces a green helper sequence and a missing required artifact. That is the same class of split as Lab 2 `accept` printing PASS without written inspections.

A mid-level engineer is trained throughout this course to run the literal command blocks. Here the literal block omits the one step that distinguishes Module 9 transfer from a lifecycle demo.

## Proposed fix

In Lab Task 1, split the block after `orient`. Tell the learner to write the `CAP-DC-01` table into `$CAPSTONE_ASSESSMENT_NOTE`, then run `activate` and `ready`. Repeat the same pause in the Windows route.

Keep helper `PASS` as the fixture transition. State explicitly that helper `PASS` on `activate` does not score CAP.1’s routing row.

Round 1 fresh open critique of issue 55 at dispatch-sha `19f2b3dd829d089519a22cfeaba8d0bbd7fb9e23`, ceiling 5768902148. Stop 1 P1 line cites re-checked on that tree. `node scripts/verify-capstone.mjs` prints `Capstone content contract: ok (36 artifacts, 0 missing)`.

The identity recut is sound. Curriculum walkthrough (`curriculum/capstone-end-to-end.md:193–198`) sends learners to the lab for literal commands and already places command-free `CAP-DC-01` before activation. Lab Task 1’s single fence then runs `orient` immediately into `activate`. Helper `activate` is the fixture transition; the scored row lives in the private note.

## 1. Task 1 is not the only lab sequence that skips the checkpoint

sharpens-framing

Evidence: `labs/capstone-end-to-end.md` Task 1 (192–208) is one fence (`orient`, `activate`, `ready`), expected `PASS`, `PASS`, `READY`, keep `orientation.json` / `scope.json` / `readiness.json`. Checkpoints rows 297–299 list those three helper verbs in order with retained proof tagged `CAP.1` and JSON only. Evidence bundle 337–349 names the private note for runtime, launcher roots, archives, and versions. Python count of `CAP-DC-01` in that lab file is 0. Existing pause shapes already in-tree: this lab’s Task 3 (250–267) splits helper fences around a learner inspect/write; `solutions/capstone-end-to-end.md` predicted evidence (79–87) inserts `[record command-free CAP-DC-01 row for CAP-DC-R1]` between `orient` and `activate`.

Failure mode: an implementer who only splits the Task 1 fence leaves Checkpoints and Evidence bundle teaching that CAP.1 proof is the three helper JSON files. A learner who uses those maps still activates immediately, the helper still prints `PASS`, and the scored row is missing.

Disposition: bind the recut as the Task 1 split plus Checkpoints retained-proof and Evidence bundle naming the private `CAP-DC-01` row between `orient` and `activate`. Reuse Task 3’s split-fence shape and the solution pause. Keep the checkpoint command-free.

## 2. The sequence lock is on assessment Task 1, not lab Task 1

sharpens-framing

Evidence: `scripts/verify-capstone.mjs:476` requires assessment Task 1 to match `install` … `orient` … `CAP-DC-01` … `activate` … `ready`. Lab checks at 500–506 require helper verb names somewhere and checkpoint helper rows equal to `stageOrder`. `scripts/verify-capstone.test.mjs` has negative cases for CAP.1 absorbing `red.json` and for a bind-ready chip; it has none for a concatenated lab Task 1 fence. Measured at this SHA: verifier exit 0 while lab `CAP-DC-01` count is 0.

Failure mode: the lab prose recut lands, a later edit concatenates Task 1 again, and `check:capstone` stays green.

Disposition: extend the existing assessment sequence assertion onto lab Task 1, with a negative test that one fence of `orient` then `activate` under that heading fails. Keep the command-free locks on curriculum, assessment, and solution (446–449).

## 3. The pause points at the existing table; Task 1’s Windows surface is one sentence

sharpens-framing

Evidence: curriculum CAP.1 (112–134) already has the empty header, passing criteria, and the hold that does not block later independently authorized fixture steps. Assessment Task 1 (70–81) already has the filled scored table, then `activate` and `ready` “in the lab’s exact order.” Lab Task 1 names PowerShell in one sentence (202–203). Full Windows fences already exist for Environment, Starting checkpoint, Reset, and Cleanup; Tasks 2–4 are Unix fences. The proposed fix says write “the CAP-DC-01 table” into `$CAPSTONE_ASSESSMENT_NOTE` and repeat the pause in the Windows route, without naming which table or which Windows surface.

Failure mode: pause text with no table still leaves a lab-as-commands learner unable to write the row (the lab file currently contains zero `CAP-DC-01`). Pasting the filled assessment row into the lab turns the recognition card into copy-from-lab. A new Task 1 PowerShell fence would be unique among the Tasks.

Disposition: the pause is a pointer to curriculum CAP.1 or assessment Task 1, written into `$CAPSTONE_ASSESSMENT_NOTE` / `$CapstoneAssessmentNote` already set at lab 78 and 121. Keep the existing PowerShell same-verbs sentence covering both verb groups after the pause.

## 4. Helper `PASS` on activate stays the fixture transition

footnote

Evidence: `activateScope` in `labs/fixtures/capstone-end-to-end/capstone-lab.mjs` (587–613) requires stage `ORIENTED`, runs promote/activate, and writes `scope.json` with `finalStatus: PASS`. It does not read the notes directory. `verify-capstone.mjs` 446–449 require the checkpoint remain command-free. Task 1 expected line 205 currently treats `PASS`, `PASS`, `READY` as the Task 1 result.

Failure mode: copying Lab 2 `accept` (PASS after attempt-from-disk inspection rows) onto capstone `activate` would put private-note bytes under the helper and recut the command-free lock. Leaving line 205 unchanged after a fence split still names helper green as Task 1 completion.

Disposition: keep helper `PASS`. Fold the expected-line change into finding 1 so helper green is the fixture transition, and the private row is the CAP.1 routing evidence.

## Road not taken

Helper-gated `activate` that requires a note path. Strongest rejected case: skip-the-prose would fail closed, matching Lab 2’s claim that `accept` waits on written inspections. Flip condition: CAP.1 stops being command-free and the note moves inside the attempt. Those are existing locks, so the recut stays a lab-prose pause using Task 3’s fence split.
